newsitem.title: USA: North American Vaccine gets UK drug trial.
newsitem.headline: North American Vaccine gets UK drug trial.

text.p: North American Vaccine on Tuesday said it has permission to begin Phase II clinical trials in Britain of its bacterial meningitis vaccine.

The drug maker said its polysaccharide conjegate vaccine, designed to protect against Group C meningococcal bacterial infections, will be administered to children in three doses beginning when they are two months old. The tests are to determine the drug's safety and its effectiveness in promoting immunity to bacterial meningitis.
Permission for the trial was granted by the Medicines Control Agency of the United Kingdom, the company said.

The new tests on infants and children follow the completion earlier this year of Phase I trials on adults, the company said. Those results indicated the drug was tolerated, produced no serious side effects, and was effective in preventing infection.
Meningococcal infection is a leading cause of bacterial meningitis. It sickened 250,000 people worldwide in 1996, killing 25,000, the company said.
It infects as many as 2,600 children and adults in the United States each year, with a fatality rate as high as 15 percent.
